sources.title: US AI chip curbs hit China tech stocks, spur self-sufficiency push
sources.excerpt: A flurry of US measures targeting China’s access to advanced AI chips further pummelled Chinese technology stocks this week, as investors weigh whether Washington’s latest curbs will slow Beijing’s ambitions or accelerate its drive for technological self-sufficiency. Chinese technology firms faced a series of new pressures, including US restrictions targeting Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips, Nvidia’s suspension of some chip shipments to China, a shareholder lawsuit against Alibaba and a US proposal that could require American companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models.
sources.limits: Reuters报道通过Investing.com转载；正文同时概述多项独立发展，本稿只聚焦远程算力限制及其影响。

sources.publisher: 美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）
sources.title: BIS Issues Rule Addressing Remote Access to American Super Intelligence Technology
sources.excerpt: WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule (IFR)—written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council—to address remote access to advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers. The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.
sources.limits: 规则背景材料，发布时间早于主新闻窗口；官方新闻稿摘要未完整列出条款细节。

sources.title: Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI technology
sources.excerpt: Under the new rule, overseas data centers that serve companies in countries including China, Russia, Iran and Cuba are required to identify their end users. There also will be additional licensing requirements for sales of chips for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil — countries that “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to unauthorized destinations, the rule says. In Beijing, China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun accused Washington of arbitrarily interfering with China's trade and technological cooperation with other countries and suppressing the development of China's high-tech industries.
sources.limits: 规则出台时的背景报道，非本刊主新闻；具体义务以BIS规则原文为准。

sources.publisher: 加利福尼亚州司法部/州检察长办公室
sources.title: Attorney General Bonta Serves Investigative Subpoena on Nvidia
sources.excerpt: OAKLAND — California Attorney General Rob Bonta today served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia related to the news of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The California Department of Justice is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public. The information received through the subpoena will help the California Department of Justice evaluate whether Nvidia’s actions violated California law.
sources.limits: 公告陈述的是调查问题和执法机关立场，不是违法认定或调查结论。

sources.title: APEC live: How events in Shenzhen unfolded
sources.excerpt: China, the U.S. and Russia will increase the production and supply of oil, and the countries promised to engage in talks that would reduce nuclear risk and prevent nuclear proliferation, according to a joint statement released by China's state news agency Xinhua. The statement, published after more than 90 minutes of discussions between the three head of states, listed four points in total. It also said the three countries would push to reform the United Nations to "more effectively address global challenges" and separately warned against overreach by the International Criminal Court.
sources.limits: 实时报道汇总会议内容；最终声明以政府公布文本为准。
